newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Lingui plans palm oil mill.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Lingui plans palm oil mill.

text.p: Malaysia's Lingui Developments Bhd said it will invest 20 million ringgit in a palm oil mill to process output from its 13,000-hectare plantation in the Borneo island state of Sabah, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.
The mill, with an annual capacity of 28 tonnes of palm oil per hectare, would be ready in 1-1/2 years when the oil palms were mature, Lingui managing director Yaw Chee Ming was quoted as saying.

He told reporters after the company's 28th annual general meeting that Lingui had acquired 9,000 hectares near the Bakun hydroelectric project in Sarawak state, also on Borneo, for oil palm plantation.
Lingui would seek more land in Sarawak to raise the area under cultivation in the two Borneo states from 22,000 hectares, Yaw said.
Demand for the company's round logs and plywood was positive, buoyed by higher prices for both commodities expected next year, he said.

For the year ended June 30, 1996, the timber division accounted for 82 percent of group turnover and contributed 70 percent of group pre-tax profit. The main demand for company products in the medium term would come from Japan, Yaw said.
